    buildPlot line and point layers

    build-plot.Rmd

    buildPlot() composes highcharter plots from table-like inputs. The common pattern is one data.table for line series and, when needed, a second data.table for point series. Both tables use ID to define the series and X/Y for coordinates.

    Line And Point Inputs

    Line data can include optional style columns such as style and fill. Point data can include marker style columns.

    library(NGR)
library(data.table)

DataLines <- data.table(
  ID = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 5),
  X = as.numeric(rep(1:5, 3)),
  Y = as.numeric(c(seq(1, 5), seq(2, 6), seq(3, 7))),
  style = c(rep("solid", 5), rep("dotted", 5), rep("dashed", 5)),
  fill = c(rep(TRUE, 5), rep(TRUE, 5), rep(FALSE, 5))
)

DataPoints <- data.table(
  ID = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 4),
  X = as.numeric(rep(1:4, 3)),
  Y = as.numeric(c(seq(8, 11), seq(6, 9), seq(4, 7))),
  style = c(rep("circle", 4), rep("diamond", 4), rep("triangle-down", 4))
)

    Combined Plot

    Pass line and point layers together. line.type = "spline" uses curved line segments while preserving the point layer.

    PLOT <- buildPlot(
  data.lines = DataLines,
  data.points = DataPoints,
  line.type = "spline",
  plot.title = "Combined Lines and Points Example",
  plot.subtitle = "Demonstration of fills, line styles, and point styles",
  plot.height = 500,
  plot.width = 700,
  xAxis.legend = "Time (units)",
  yAxis.legend = "Value",
  print.max.abs = FALSE
)

PLOT

    Required Columns

    For line series:

    Column Role
    ID series identifier
    X x coordinate
    Y y coordinate

    For point series, the same ID, X, and Y columns are required. Optional columns such as style, size, fill, or yAxis are consumed when present by the plotting helper.

    Related Articles

    Use the secondary-axis article when the plot needs a linked or independent right-hand axis. Use the gridline-theme article when plotting on log axes.
